text: What did Great-Grandma say about a closed mouth?
It never gets fed.
What did Great-Grandma say about people talking behind your back?
It means you're ahead of them.
What did Great-Grandma say about wrestling with a pig?
You both get dirty, but the pig likes it.
What did Great-Grandma say about throwing stones?
Only trees with the best fruit get rocks thrown at them.
What did Great-Grandma say about crying over spilled milk?
Clean it up so nobody slips on it.
What did Great-Grandma say about changing a bad man?
The only thing you'll change is your mind.
What did Great-Grandma say about a watched pot?
It cooks just fine if you leave the kitchen.
What did Great-Grandma say about a loud dog?
The ones that bark the loudest are the easiest to outrun.
What did Great-Grandma say about chasing a dollar?
If you run too fast, it'll spend you before you spend it.
What did Great-Grandma say about putting shoes on a horse?
It doesn't make him a gentleman.
What did Great-Grandma say about waiting for the perfect weather?
You'll end up starving in the shade.
What did Great-Grandma say about the neighbors' opinions?
They don't buy your groceries, so don't let them cook your dinner.
What did Great-Grandma say about trying to argue with a fool?
From a distance, nobody can tell which one is which.
What did Great-Grandma say about dogs barking at the moon?
The moon keeps on shining anyway.
What did Great-Grandma say about looking back too long?
You'll trip over what's right in front of you.
What did Great-Grandma say about a snake shedding its skin?
It's still got the same bite.
What did Great-Grandma say about an empty wagon?
It makes the most noise going down the road.
What did Great-Grandma say about hoarding every penny?
Shrouds don't come with pockets.
What did Great-Grandma say about painting a rotten fence?
The wood's still snapping under the coat.
What did Great-Grandma say about how they treat their mother?
That's the preview for the main attraction.
What did Great-Grandma say about a mate who only speaks in sweet talk?
Sugar dissolves the minute the rain starts.
What did Great-Grandma say about someone who treats the waiter poorly?
Hold onto your purse and walk out the door.
What did Great-Grandma say about a partner who is always the victim?
If they're always fighting dragons, they might be the ones lighting the fire.
What did Great-Grandma say about a partner who is nice to everyone but you?
A street angel makes a house devil.
What did Great-Grandma say about marrying for looks alone?
The prettiest plate doesn't put food on the table.
What did Great-Grandma say about marrying for money?
You'll earn every single penny the hard way.
What did Great-Grandma say about choosing a partner for hard times?
Pick the one you'd want holding the flashlights when the storm hits.
What did Great-Grandma say about looking for perfection?
If you want an angel, you better build heaven first.
What did Great-Grandma say about sharing a roof?
Don't marry someone you can live with; marry the one you can't live without.
What did Great-Grandma say about trying to change a mate after marriage?
You aren't buying a fixer-upper; you're moving into the house as it stands.
What did Great-Grandma say about ignoring your gut feeling?
If your stomach feels uneasy, don't blame the cooking.
What did Great-Grandma say about chasing someone who runs away?
Save your shoes; let them keep walking.
What did Great-Grandma say about a mate who keeps secrets?
Where there's smoke, the basement is already on fire.
What did Great-Grandma say about rushing into love?
The faster the fire burns, the quicker you're left with ashes.
What did Great-Grandma say about keeping score in arguments?
If you both try to win, the marriage loses.
What did Great-Grandma say about going to bed angry?
Stay up and fight it out so you can sleep in peace.
What did Great-Grandma say about airing your marriage troubles to the neighbors?
Keep your laundry in your own yard.
What did Great-Grandma say about the secret to a long marriage?
Two good forgivers living under one roof.
What did Great-Grandma say about a happy home?
It requires a lot of love, a little bit of space, and plenty of good food.
What did Great-Grandma say about telling a lie?
You better have a fantastic memory, because the truth remembers itself.
What did Great-Grandma say about sugarcoating the truth?
A bitter pill cures the illness; a sweet one just rots your teeth.
What did Great-Grandma say about someone who whispers the truth?
The truth doesn't need a megaphone to shake the room.
What did Great-Grandma say about pretending to be something you're not?
An honest penny is worth more than a counterfeit dollar.
What did Great-Grandma say about people who don't like honest words?
The truth only hurts when it's supposed to.
What did Great-Grandma say about trying to speed up time?
You can't bake a three-hour cake in twenty minutes just by turning up the oven.
What did Great-Grandma say about waiting for your turn?
The sun doesn't rush the moon, and they both get a chance to shine.
What did Great-Grandma say about a seed in the dirt?
Digging it up every day to check on it won't make it grow any faster.
What did Great-Grandma say about losing your temper?
A moment of patience saves a lifetime of clean-up.
What did Great-Grandma say about the longest winter?
The snow always melts, no matter how much it likes the ground.
What did Great-Grandma say about giving advice?
Don't sweep my porch until you've scrubbed your own kitchen floor.
What did Great-Grandma say about a loud sermon?
I'd rather see a good example than hear a long speech.
What did Great-Grandma say about pointing fingers?
When you're busy pointing at someone else, three fingers are pointing right back at you.
What did Great-Grandma say about a guide who won't walk the trail?
Don't take directions from someone who hasn't left the front porch.
What did Great-Grandma say about leading the way?
If you want the pack to follow, you better be willing to carry the heaviest load.
What did Great-Grandma say about hitting a wall?
The wall is just there to see if you're willing to find a ladder.
What did Great-Grandma say about a bad day?
The sunset is proof that even the hardest days have an ending.
What did Great-Grandma say about falling down?
As long as you land looking up, you can get back up.
What did Great-Grandma say about a rough sea?
A smooth ocean never made a skilled captain.
What did Great-Grandma say about a slow start?
It doesn't matter how slow you walk, as long as you don't turn around.
What did Great-Grandma say about planting thorns?
Don't expect to harvest roses when you've been scattering weeds.
What did Great-Grandma say about how you treat the ground?
The earth gives back exactly what you put into it, plus interest.
What did Great-Grandma say about throwing dirt?
You're the one who ends up with dirty hands.
What did Great-Grandma say about kindness?
Scatter the seeds generously; you'll need the shade later on.
What did Great-Grandma say about a lazy spring?
If you sleep through the planting, don't look for a bowl at the harvest.
What did Great-Grandma say about true strength?
Speak softly so they have to listen close, but keep your boots laced tight.
What did Great-Grandma say about a quiet person?
Still water runs deep, and it can move a mountain if it wants to.
What did Great-Grandma say about showing your cards?
Let them guess what's in your pocket until it's time to pay the bill.
What did Great-Grandma say about empty threats?
Never raise your fist if you aren't ready to use your hands.
What did Great-Grandma say about keeping your cool?
A gentle smile hides a sharp mind perfectly.
What did Great-Grandma say about a flattering friend?
I'd rather have an honest slap in the face than a deceitful kiss on the cheek.
What did Great-Grandma say about a hard message?
Don't blame the mirror just because you don't like the reflection.
What did Great-Grandma say about keeping quiet when it matters?
Silence in the face of a lie is just a lie with its mouth shut.
What did Great-Grandma say about telling it like it is?
If it looks like a skunk and smells like a skunk, don't call it a kitten.
What did Great-Grandma say about standing alone with the truth?
An honest lone wolf is safer than a pack of wolves pretending to be sheep.
What did Great-Grandma say about carrying a heavy burden?
The load doesn't break you; it's the way you carry it.
What did Great-Grandma say about a storm coming?
Don't pray for the rain to stop; pray for a stronger umbrella.
What did Great-Grandma say about a sharp tongue?
Keep your words soft and sweet, because you never know which ones you'll have to eat.
What did Great-Grandma say about shortcuts?
The longest distance between two points is a shortcut.
What did Great-Grandma say about old age?
The wrinkles just show where the smiles and the battles used to be.
What did Great-Grandma say about a young mind?
A spongy sponge holds the most water.
What did Great-Grandma say about making a mistake?
That's just tuition paid to the school of life.
What did Great-Grandma say about asking questions?
The only silly question is the one you took home with you.
What did Great-Grandma say about trying something new?
You'll never know if you can play the fiddle until you pick up the bow.
What did Great-Grandma say about an old dog?
You can absolutely teach him new tricks if the treat is good enough.
What did Great-Grandma say about a slow learner?
The oak tree takes its time, but it outlasts the weeds.
What did Great-Grandma say about listening?
You have two ears and one mouth for a very good reason.
What did Great-Grandma say about change?
If you don't shed your old feathers, you'll never get to grow new ones.
What did Great-Grandma say about an expert?
He's just a beginner who didn't throw in the towel.
What did Great-Grandma say about looking at the stars?
It reminds your feet how far they can actually walk.
What did Great-Grandma say about a curious child?
Keep him asking 'why' and he'll eventually figure out 'how'.
What did Great-Grandma say about staying in your comfort zone?
A ship in the harbor is safe, but that's not what ships are built for.
What did Great-Grandma say about a rough patch?
The diamond only gets shiny after a whole lot of rubbing.
What did Great-Grandma say about wisdom?
It's the one thing you can pack in your suitcase that doesn't weigh a pound.
What did Great-Grandma say about growing older?
You aren't adding years; you're just collecting beautiful chapters.
What did Great-Grandma say when things were already going great?
The cream always rises right to the top.
What did Great-Grandma say about a good streak of luck?
When the wind is at your back, spread your wings and fly.
What did Great-Grandma say about finding a little success?
That's just the appetizer; the feast is still on the stove.
What did Great-Grandma say about a beautiful sunrise?
The day is only going to get brighter from here.
What did Great-Grandma say about a small win?
A single spark can start a whole celebration.
What did Great-Grandma say about a good idea?
Once the wheel starts turning, you can't stop the momentum.
What did Great-Grandma say about making a little progress?
Every step forward makes the next one twice as easy.
What did Great-Grandma say about a joyful home?
There's always room for more laughter under this roof.
What did Great-Grandma say about a sweet moment?
Honey only gets sweeter the longer it sits.
What did Great-Grandma say about a budding talent?
You've got the seed, now watch the whole garden bloom.
What did Great-Grandma say about catching a big fish?
There's always a bigger one waiting out in the deep water.
What did Great-Grandma say about a joyful heart?
Joy is a well that never runs out of water.
What did Great-Grandma say about a good harvest?
Next year's barns are going to need to be twice as big.
What did Great-Grandma say about a clear blue sky?
It's a wide-open road all the way to the horizon.
What did Great-Grandma say about a celebration?
Keep the music playing; the best song hasn't even started yet.
